as_title: Digital Technologies 1.2 Develop a digital technologies outcome

keyTerminologyAndClarifications.definition: The final product or result of a process.
keyTerminologyAndClarifications.clarification: In this context, it refers to the digital product created by the student, such as a programmed system, electronic device, web application, or print media solution.

keyTerminologyAndClarifications.definition: The suitability of an outcome to meet its intended use.
keyTerminologyAndClarifications.clarification: The outcome must meet the specifications, serve the needs of its intended users, and function reliably in its intended context.

keyTerminologyAndClarifications.definition: The process of examining an outcome to ensure it functions correctly.
keyTerminologyAndClarifications.clarification: Students test their own digital outcome or parts of it to ensure basic functionality before user trialling.

keyTerminologyAndClarifications.definition: Having others use the outcome to assess its suitability.
keyTerminologyAndClarifications.clarification: Involves end users using the outcome to determine its fitness for purpose and providing feedback for improvements.

keyTerminologyAndClarifications.definition: Established practices within a specific domain.
keyTerminologyAndClarifications.clarification: Refers to the standard practices in the digital technologies domain being used, such as programming syntax, interface design standards, circuit labeling, or layout principles in print media.

keyTerminologyAndClarifications.definition: In the best way practicable for a task.
keyTerminologyAndClarifications.clarification: Tools or techniques are applied in the most effective manner for the task, showing deliberate and skilled application to improve quality and performance.

gradingCriteria.mainRequirement: Fails to meet the minimum requirements for Achievement
evidenceFocusPoints: The outcome does not address the requirements and specifications.
Basic functionality of the outcome is not demonstrated.
If the purpose, potential users, or specifications are not described, this sublevel cannot be awarded.
No evidence of testing or trialling is present.
gradingCriteria.exampleClarification: A digital project that lacks a clear description of its purpose and fails to function as intended.

gradingCriteria.mainRequirement: Produces an outcome that meets basic requirements and specifications.
criteriaInvolves: Describing the purpose, potential users, requirements, and specifications of the outcome.
Using appropriate tools or techniques to produce an outcome.
Testing the outcome to ensure basic functionality.
evidenceFocusPoints: The outcome addresses the basic requirements and specifications.
The purpose and potential users are clearly described.
Basic functionality is demonstrated through testing.
If testing is not documented, this sublevel cannot be awarded.
A4 requires a thorough and well-structured description of requirements and specifications, while A3 may include a more basic or partially developed explanation.
gradingCriteria.exampleClarification: A student creates a simple app or electronic system that meets the outlined requirements and functions correctly after testing.

gradingCriteria.mainRequirement: Refines the outcome to improve its fitness for purpose.
criteriaInvolves: Following conventions relevant to the digital technologies domain.
Using information from testing to make improvements.
evidenceFocusPoints: The outcome is refined based on testing feedback.
Conventions specific to the relevant digital technologies domain (e.g., programming, circuit design, UI layout, print formatting) are followed.
Improvements enhance the outcome's fitness for purpose.
If conventions are not followed, this sublevel cannot be awarded.
M6 requires more significant or targeted improvements based on testing compared to M5.
gradingCriteria.exampleClarification: A student refines their irrigation monitoring system by calibrating sensors and improving layout based on test results, following relevant digital conventions.

gradingCriteria.mainRequirement: Enhances the outcome to optimally meet the requirements and specifications.
criteriaInvolves: Using information from trialling with others to improve fitness for purpose.
evidenceFocusPoints: The outcome is enhanced to optimally meet specifications.
Trialling with end users is documented and used for further improvements.
Tools and techniques are applied in the best way practicable.
If trialling feedback is not used for enhancement, this sublevel cannot be awarded.
E8 requires comprehensive enhancements and optimal application of techniques compared to E7.
gradingCriteria.exampleClarification: A student enhances their plant monitoring app by integrating real-time data visualisation and alert systems, based on feedback from trial users, ensuring performance and usability are optimal.

finalInstructionForLLM: Evaluate the student work against the criteria and evidence focus points for each band and sublevel. Award the highest grade/sublevel for which all required evidence is present. If not achieved, state which criteria/evidence was missing. Justify the decision using explicit references to the student work and clarify which sublevel was awarded and why.
